corrected_verdict: KNOWN. Classical in convex analysis (Rockafellar Sec. 32) and standard in the ML/sparse-optimization literature: Mangasarian 1996/1999 concave-minimization feature selection; Ge-Jiang-Ye 2011, where l_p (p<1) local minimizers over {Ax=b,x>=0} are exactly the basic feasible solutions. The current proof in app:shape (i) is self-contained, so a citation is optional but recommended for positioning.
issues: (1) STALE TARGET. appendix.tex:134 no longer contains 'Hence the minimum is attained at a vertex.' Proof (i) now gets existence from compact sublevel sets (v_j <= phi(v)^{1/r}) and then uses the midpoint/strict-concavity argument. It no longer calls on the concave-nondecreasing/line-free vertex theorem, so the item statement is stale and the checker's recommended_change cannot be applied as written. The proof is correct. (2) MISSED ML PRIOR ART. min sum_j v_j^{1/s} (1/s<1) over P_p is l_r quasi-norm/concave-penalty minimization over a polyhedron in the orthant. The vertex property in exactly this form is the classical concave-penalty sparsity mechanism in ML: Mangasarian 1996 (feature selection as polyhedral concave minimization, 'By [Rockafellar, Corollary 32.3.4] ... f attains its minimum at a vertex'); Mangasarian 1999 (ML-motivated minimum-support vertex solutions, Lemma 2.2); and Ge-Jiang-Ye 2011 (preprint Thm 3: basic feasible solutions = local minimizers of sum x_j^p, 0<p<1, and the proof's second half is the paper's midpoint argument). None of this threatens the paper's claims, whose novelty is the reduction and the structure of P_p. But the paper never mentions the l_p/concave-penalty connection, and an ML reviewer will. One sentence near Prop. shapes/bottleneck is recommended. (3) CONFIRMED CITATIONS SURVIVE ON METADATA. Rockafellar: Crossref DOI 10.1515/9781400873173, PUP 1970; Princeton page shows Princeton Mathematical Series but not vol. 28. Horst-Tuy: Crossref DOI 10.1007/978-3-662-03199-5, 1996; subtitle 'Deterministic Approaches' via OpenLibrary; 1990/1993/1996 editions put it at the 3rd. The Sec. 32 text is still unfetched. New secondary evidence: two Mangasarian papers independently cite Rockafellar Cor. 32.3.4 (vertex) and Cor. 32.3.3 (existence) for exactly this statement. So 'Sec. 32' is safe, and 'Cor. 32.3.4' is very likely right but should be checked in the book before printing. (4) Ge-Jiang-Ye theorem number is from the 2009 Jiang-Ye preprint; the published author list adds Ge, and published numbering is unverified. Cite without a theorem number. (5) New recommended edit: at the end of proof (i) add '(This is the classical vertex property of concave minimization over a line-free polyhedron \citep[Sec.~32]{rockafellar1970convex}; for $\ell_r$ objectives with $r<1$ see also \citet{ge2011note}.)'. Optionally in cyclic.tex after P_p add: 'Minimizing $\sum_j v_j^{1/s}$, $1/s<1$, over a polyhedron is a concave problem whose minimizers are vertices, the mechanism behind concave-penalty feature selection \citep{mangasarian1996machine,mangasarian1999minimum} and $\ell_p$ sparse recovery \citep{ge2011note}; what is specific here is $\curlyp_p$.' Horst-Tuy is optional. Process note: the WebSearch budget is exhausted, so all sources were reached by direct URL.

extra_citations.why: An ML-motivated statement that concave minimization over a polyhedral set has a vertex solution, with minimum support. Lemma 2.2 assumes a concave function bounded below on a line-free polyhedral set and cites Rockafellar Cor. 32.3.3 & 32.3.4. Metadata is Crossref-confirmed, and the text was read from UW tech report 97-05. It supports the vertex step and positions Prop. shapes/bottleneck against the classical concave-penalty sparsity mechanism.

It poses feature selection as minimizing a concave function bounded below over {Ax<=b, x>=0} and states 'By [Rockafellar, Corollary 32.3.4] it follows that f attains its minimum at a vertex of the feasible region'. This is the ML precedent for 'concave cost over a polyhedron => vertex => sparse features'. Metadata is Crossref-confirmed, and the text was read from UW tech report 95-20.

For min sum_j x_j^p (0<p<1) over {Ax=b, x>=0}, the basic feasible solutions are exactly the local minimizers, so every minimizer is a vertex. The proof uses the same strict-concavity/midpoint argument as app:shape (i). It is the closest match to the paper's l_{1/s} objective. Metadata is Crossref-confirmed; the text was read from the 2009 preprint (Theorem 3 there). Cite without a theorem number.
